paper_title: Constraining hidden photons via atomic force microscope measurements and the Plimpton-Lawton experiment
notes: Paper derives two new laboratory hidden-photon (kinetic mixing chi) bounds: (1) from AFM Casimir-force measurements, excluding chi >~ 10^-0.5 for masses ~0.1-10 eV (weaker bound, not emitted here), and (2) from the 1936 Plimpton-Lawton concentric-shell Coulomb's-law test, which is the stronger and wider result (purple curve in Figs. 1 and 7). No numerical table is provided; the emitted data points were computed from the paper's closed-form expression Eq. (26) with the stated parameters R*=0.61 m, R=0.76 m, and sensitivity gamma=3.3e-10, including the asymptotic limits Eqs. (27a,b). Text confirms the low-mass cutoff at m~0.02 neV (chi->1) consistent with computed points. Paper also gives projections (Figs. 6, 8) with improved sensitivity gamma=1e-15, not included here. No confidence level explicitly stated (null-result reinterpretation); no DM density assumption (not a DM haloscope). | selector: text (sole candidate) | axis-peek for confusable-family text read (#625 Phase 3c)
